newsitem.title: KENYA: Uganda plans arabica export auctions - trade.
newsitem.headline: Uganda plans arabica export auctions - trade.

text.p: Uganda plans to launch coffee export auctions for its arabicas on the same lines as Kenya's, traders in the capital Kampala said on Wednesday.
They said the Uganda Coffee Development Authority was working on the details of such an auction, which would handle 12 percent of Uganda's total crop.
Around 88 percent of the country's production is robusta.
"They are working on auction details, drawing a lot from Kenya's experience," a trader told Reuters by telephone.
Kenya holds a weekly export auction for its arabicas.
Ugandan officials believe they may also be able to tap Burundian coffee, often offloaded at the Nairobi auction, and Rwandan arabicas when they launches the auction, a trader said.
"At the moment, no date has been pegged on when the auctions will begin but authorities are looking at an early date next year," a senior Ugandan coffee official said.
"We cannot say whether it will be weekly, twice-a-month as in Tanzania or monthly yet. We have to study how our supply equation will meet demand on the auction floor," he added.
